text:
I have no time to look at things

as I desire.

They slip over my gaze,

and all that I see

are deep corners labeled with radio,

where I read the city so as not to lose time.

This forced haste that inexorably

wants to hand me the world with a small datum.

This urgent looking and this voice in a smile

for a young man who knows how to die for every dream.

I have no time to look at things,

I almost guess them.

An innate and jealous wisdom

gives me prior glances and sudden trills.

I live on golden margins; I ignore the central joy

of things. I unfold centuries of gold in my being.

And, accelerating gusts—keel or golden wing—,

I make up the sweet time I shall never have.

translation.title: I Have No Time to Look at Things...
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps Pellicer's hurried perception and the odd 'radio' labeling image from the source.
